skill.name: backend-models
skill.description: Define and configure database models with proper naming, relationships, timestamps, data types, constraints, and validation. Use this skill when creating or editing model files in app/Models/, Eloquent model classes, model relationships (hasMany, belongsTo, etc.), database table structures, model attributes and casts, model factories, or seeders. Use when working on model validation logic, database constraints, foreign key relationships, indexes, scopes, accessors, mutators, or any ORM-related model configuration.
skill.summary: Guide backend model design for ORM relationships, attributes, validation, factories, and database constraints.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The external command finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a path, with no command execution. The filesystem finding is confirmed because SKILL.md points agents to a parent-directory file outside the skill package using ../../../. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or other semantic abuse was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Inline the required model standards or include the referenced file inside the skill package, then link to it without parent-directory traversal.

finding_verdicts.reason: The static hit is Markdown inline code around app/Models/, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. SKILL.md contains no executable command or command invocation at this location.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent model definitions that match database and ORM standards. This skill guides AI assistants through model naming, relationships, casts, validation, factories, and seeders.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and editing of model files under app/Models/ and similar directories.
Covers Eloquent relationships including hasMany, belongsTo, belongsToMany, hasOne, and morphTo.
Provides direction for casts, fillable fields, hidden attributes, timestamps, and soft deletes.
Supports model validation logic, scopes, accessors, mutators, events, and observers.
Includes guidance areas for factories, seeders, database constraints, foreign keys, and indexes.
limitations: The detailed standards are delegated to an external relative Markdown link.
It does not include executable generators or migration automation.
It does not validate a real database schema without project context.
It focuses on ORM model configuration, not controller or API design.

use_cases.title: Create Project Models
use_cases.description: Draft model definitions with names, attributes, relationships, timestamps, casts, and validation needs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test Data
use_cases.description: Plan factories and seeders that match model attributes, relationships, and database constraints.

use_cases.title: Review Model Consistency
use_cases.description: Check existing model files for relationship accuracy, fillable fields, hidden attributes, scopes, and soft delete setup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to draft an Eloquent model for [entity] with fillable fields [fields] and timestamps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Relationships and Casts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to update [model] with relationships to [related models], casts for [fields], and hidden attributes for [fields].

prompt_templates.title: Review Model Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to review [model] against these migration details: [summary]. Check constraints, indexes, validation, and scopes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Model Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to design models for [feature]. Include entities, relationships, casts, validation rules, factories, seeders, indexes, and observer needs.

output_examples.input: Review a Customer model with orders, soft deletes, and hidden personal fields.
output: Identifies the needed orders relationship and ownership direction.
Recommends hidden personal fields and appropriate casts.
Checks soft delete setup and related index considerations.

output_examples.input: Plan models, factories, and seeders for a subscription billing feature.
output: Lists core entities and their relationship types.
Describes factory data needed for reliable tests.
Calls out validation and constraint checks before implementation.

best_practices: Provide table names, key fields, and relationship cardinality before asking for model changes.
Ask for casts, fillable fields, hidden attributes, and validation rules in the same model review.
Confirm model guidance against migrations and database constraints before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to infer private schema details without project context.
Do not treat model guidance as a substitute for migration or database review.
Do not reference missing external standard files without sharing the relevant rules.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets backend ORM model work, with explicit references to Laravel Eloquent patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate migrations?
faq.answer: It can guide model-related database constraints and indexes, but it does not provide migration automation.

faq.question: Does it handle model relationships?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common relationships such as hasMany, belongsTo, belongsToMany, hasOne, and morphTo.

faq.question: Can it help with test data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for model factories and seeders used in testing or seeding.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide entity names, fields, table details, relationship rules, validation needs, and database constraints.

faq.question: Is the skill self-contained?
faq.answer: Not fully. The current skill references a standards file outside the skill package.
